_help: Edit text here (or in the studio), then run: node shared/build.mjs instagram (from design/carousels). Markup: *word* = accent colour, _word_ = serif italic, \n = line break. A slide's own "accent" overrides the deck accent for that slide only.

slides.title:
Anyone in
Ghana can
look up
your
*marriage.*
slides.sub: Marriages and divorces are now searchable on a new public app, Marrify. Who should be able to see them?

slides.title:
Type a name,
see their marriage
*record.*
slides.takeaway: Divorce records too, some reportedly going back to 1886.

slides.title:
Is a divorce
really *public?*

cards.s: In Estonia, anyone can check it. A business answers to the public.
In Ghana, now searchable by name.

slides.takeaway: I like open data. I just don’t know yet how that works with personal records like these.

slides.title:
Public in theory.
Now one search
*away.*

rows.s: A divorce file in a courthouse somewhere
The same record, on a stranger’s phone, in seconds

slides.takeaway: Did the people in these records ever agree to that kind of reach?

slides.title:
What if the app
only answered
what was *asked?*
slides.q: Is this person free to marry?
slides.takeaway: That’s data minimisation: show the least data that answers the question.

slides.title:
Not everyone
needs the
*same* view.
slides.takeaway:
Who decides which organisations
get the fuller view?

slides.title:
Same
record.
*Different*
weight.
slides.body: In Estonia, a divorce record can be just admin. In many African contexts, divorce still carries stigma, especially for women.
slides.note: “It’s not just a privacy engineering conversation. It’s also a cultural design thing.”

slides.title:
If someone looks
you up, do you get
to *see* that?
slides.head: Imagined access log
slides.takeaway: In Estonia, I can see what happens to my data in the system. Could Ghana do that too?

slides.title:
“Centralised
data.
_Finally._”
slides.body: I’m Nigerian and I’ve lived in Estonia for a year. One reliable record solves so many problems. So yes, part of me wants this.

cols.v: A link for everything, even marriage and divorce.

slides.corner: // my first thought, as an African

slides.title:
I want Africa
building _this._
slides.body: And questioning it while we do.
slides.video: Ghana Launched an App to Check If Someone Is Married
slides.ask: Send this to someone in Ghana.
